content.description_p1: In physics, force is an interaction that can change the motion of an object. The SI unit is the Newton (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton. Imperial systems use pound-force (lbf), while kilogram-force (kgf) is used in some technical contexts.
content.description_p2: Kilonewtonlar (kN), yapısal yükler gibi büyük kuvvetler için kullanılır (1 kN = 1000 N). Dinler mikroskobik ölçeklerde kullanılır. Bu ilişkileri anlamak havacılık, inşaat mühendisliği ve temel fizik için hayati önem taşır. Not: Dünya'da 1 kgf ≈ 9,81 N.

content.faq_q1: What is the difference between a Newton and Kilogram-force?
content.faq_a1: A Newton is an absolute unit; kilogram-force depends on gravity. On Earth, 1 kg mass exerts about 9.81 Newtons of force.
content.faq_q2: How many Newtons are in a pound-force?
content.faq_a2: One pound-force (lbf) equals approximately 4.448 Newtons. This is a common calculation for converting US engineering standards.
content.faq_a3: Kilonewtons are used where large forces are measured, such as civil engineering, climbing gear, and industrial presses. 1 kN = 1000 N.
content.faq_q4: Is force the same as mass?
content.faq_a4: No. Mass (kg) is the amount of matter; force (N) is the effect on that matter due to gravity or acceleration. F = m × a.
